## Solving for the Odds Ratio

In this demonstration, we sample 6000 male and 6500 female patients and count the number of cases for multiple cancers including: Non-small cell lung cancer, Basal Cell Carcinoma, and Pancreatic Cancer.  We then calculate the Odds Ratio between Men and Women for each of the cancer groups and illustrate the results.

```{r Odds-Ratio, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Load libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Data
N_male   <- 6000
N_female <- 6500

df <- data.frame(
  Cancer = c("Osteosarcoma",
             "Glioblastoma",
             "Invasive lobular carcinoma",
             "Pancreatic cancer",
             "Retinoblastoma",
             "Basal cell carcinoma",
             "Non-small cell lung cancer"),
  Male_cases   = c(10, 30, 5, 90, 5, 140, 220),
  Female_cases = c(8, 20, 200, 80, 4, 160, 180)
)

# Compute noncases
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    Male_noncases   = N_male - Male_cases,
    Female_noncases = N_female - Female_cases
  )

# Compute odds ratio
df <- df %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    OR = (Male_cases * Female_noncases) / (Female_cases * Male_noncases)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Order by descending OR
df <- df %>% arrange(desc(OR))

# Plot horizontal bar chart
ggplot(df, aes(x = OR, y = reorder(Cancer, OR))) +
  geom_col(fill = "blue") +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = c("blue", "black", "red"),
    name = "Odds Ratio"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Odds Ratio (Male vs Female) by Cancer Type",
    x = "Odds Ratio (log scale optional)",
    y = "Cancer Type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

```
